newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Shorts outshine the U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Shorts outshine the U.S..

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads to the dollar bloc were fairly mixed, but the local short end put in another solid performance against the U.S. and Canada.
Fears of a tightening by the Federal Reserve in July were renewed as U.S. consumer confidence rose to its highest level in 28 years and hit North American markets on Tuesday.

The local short end, however, continues to find demand after last week's official interest rate cut to 5.5 percent and the three-year yield differential to the U.S. went negative, a move that had already been accomplished by shorter maturities.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread widened slightly after the market found resistance on nearing last week's three-year low of around 75 basis points.
Meanwhile, New Zealand bonds held their ground, underpinned by talk of further issuance of Eurokiwi or samurai bonds linked to the N.Z. dollar.
